rationale: The flagged item is the only anomalous transaction on an otherwise stable in-person card: 69 of 71 baseline txns are in-person (online share 2.8%, product C share 1.4%), and the $74.96 online purchase came from a Samsung SM-G935F/Chrome-for-Android profile flagged New for this account behind an anonymous IP proxy. That exact device string is shared by 52 cards all-time and 20 cards in this window, and eight of those linked cards carry confirmed fraud cases; four closed cases in memory (CC-2985, CC-2971, CC-2649, CC-3035) are cardholders who reported online purchases they did not make from this same SM-G935F/anonymous-proxy profile, all closed as confirmed_fraud with the undocumented pattern. The low model score (0.05) is not exculpatory — it is a reason to look, not a verdict, and this device ring has repeatedly scored low. The surrounding in-person txns (3477218 in region 191, 3478886 in region 272) match the cardholder's normal home activity and are not part of the episode. Because this is a single disputed-value transaction rather than a customer report, I sought validation; given the memory precedent the customer almost certainly denies the online charge.
